hypothesis: A versioned replayable commit envelope plus durable request-outcome reconstruction can make Cell v0 lost-reply, resolver, log-tag, generation, and quorum invariants executable before a production WAL exists.
learned: Recovery must rebuild both retained client outcomes and the previous committed log-chain head; the envelope must carry replayable conflict and mutation payloads rather than only their digest.

hypothesis: A logical row oracle can freeze exact base-plus-tail semantics, snapshot retention, and certified-write validation before a DataFusion physical operator exists.
learned: Invalidation must precede predicate and projection; analytical-tail GC is independent from recovery-WAL pop; an active lease fixes object closure; dependency validation and write must be one serializable transaction.

hypothesis: A versioned checksummed local frame plus per-file synchronization and matching-quorum reconstruction can persist the frozen commit envelope, rebuild retained retry outcomes after fresh opens, and reject unsafe suffixes before a consensus library is selected.
learned: Quorum durability should be reconstructed from matching bytes rather than trusted from a self-declared disk certificate; incomplete final frames may be ignored, while complete corruption without a remaining quorum and envelope-chain disagreement must halt recovery. Consensus, network replication, elections, and independent failure domains remain unproven.

hypothesis: An objectKV-owned append-only per-node journal can satisfy OpenRaft 0.9.25 storage-v2 semantics and recover durable vote, committed position, append, conflicting-suffix truncate, purge, and corruption state across fresh opens before networked consensus exists.
learned: The consensus library expects obsolete appends below the durable purge marker to be harmless and same-or-lower retained suffix appends to durably replace that suffix. The objectKV journal can encode both safely while rejecting gaps above the retained log. This admits per-node stable storage only; quorum commit, elections, network faults, generation takeover, and real process crash remain unproven.

hypothesis: Three OpenRaft nodes using objectKV per-node journals and a seeded Turmoil TCP network can preserve quorum-acknowledged commits through leader isolation, successor election, partition repair, stale-suffix replacement, simulated process crash, bounce, and restarted-node catchup.
learned: A single explicit election trigger can arrive before the prior committed-vote lease permits takeover; the deterministic controller must keep the event explicit while retriggering until the recorded successor state is observed. The cluster safely replaces an isolated uncommitted suffix after a higher-term quorum commits. This admits simulated runtime crash and real-journal reopen only; real OS process kill, unsynced-disk loss, generation takeover, and durable request-outcome integration remain unproven.

hypothesis: A versioned request identity and replay-built outcome inside the replicated OpenRaft application history can survive a lost reply, real leader-process kill, successor retry, and killed-node restart without applying the logical command twice.
learned: A durable retry outcome can be rebuilt by replaying the committed log into a fresh state machine, but the eval must wait through the duplicate log index before judging recovered state or it can sample midway through replay. This admits normal TCP and real OS process death; state-machine snapshot persistence, outcome expiry, automatic election, generation takeover, independent-disk loss, and object-store recovery remain unproven.

hypothesis: A replicated external authority plus a data-log fence barrier can move one cell from Active through Fencing and Recovering, reject a preauthorized G1 write ordered after the barrier, survive authority-leader loss, hand the voter set from G1 to G2, and resume with one exact log.
learned: An external linearizable authority read alone has a cross-consensus TOCTOU window. The old transaction system must also commit a replicated data-log fence barrier, and its state machine must reject stale client entries ordered after that barrier before recovery is reserved. This admits a quiesced real-process voter-set takeover. Automatic failure detection, authenticated fence and recovery certificates, control-root reconciliation, coordinator membership change, independent-disk loss, and object-store recovery remain unproven.

hypothesis: Distinct data voters can sign exact locally applied fence and voter-set positions so the external generation authority can reject controller-fabricated recovery evidence before reserving or activating a transaction-system generation.
learned: A signer must attest the exact applied barrier or voter-set transition, not merely a lower position it has applied past. The certificate must bind purpose, cell, generation, recovery identity, active and pending transaction-system identities, membership, and Raft position. Real-process election terms can vary across replays, so the semantic trace normalizes terms while certificate verification still binds the exact observed term. Production key custody, control-root reconciliation, and independent-disk recovery remain unproven.

hypothesis: A custom DataFusion TableProvider and ExecutionPlan can preserve the frozen exact-snapshot contract across a schema-v1 Parquet base and schema-v2 Arrow tail before streaming or pruning optimizations exist.
learned: DataFusion still pushes output projection into a scan when filters remain unsupported, so the provider must add projection above the hidden-column overlay. Its Parquet reader defaults strings to Utf8View, which the v1-to-v2 normalizer must either accept or explicitly disable. DataFusion 54.0 also admits incompatible 54.1 internal crates unless the complete family is lockfile-pinned. The exact physical contract is possible, but this correctness adapter materializes bounded inputs and admits no performance curve yet.

hypothesis: A transactional publication intent, named immutable-object verification, complete reachability walk, quarantine interval, and delete-time root-domain revalidation can prevent premature visibility and live-object deletion despite unknown PUT outcomes, GC races, counter drift, stale LIST responses, interrupted marks, and root changes.
learned: An uploaded block needs a transactional in-flight root before GC can race it. Accounting counters and LIST observations cannot determine liveness, a partial mark reclaims nothing, and every delete plan must be revalidated after a root-epoch change. This deterministic model admits the contract only; a real object client, durable transactional authority, independent process failure, and guarded delete worker remain unproven.

hypothesis: A DataFusion execution plan can merge schema-normalized Parquet base rows and Arrow table changes incrementally across arbitrary record-batch boundaries, preserve one target version across independent partition watermarks and continuation, and declare ordered output without materializing either complete input.
learned: With skewed physical-partition bases, the first exact global identity stream must read the tail from min(W_p), even though that replays changes already reflected in newer bases. Logical-id reduction must cross Arrow batch boundaries, continuation must retain T, and output ordering is safe to declare only after validating both input orders across batches. This admits bounded operator buffering and exactness only; manifest and lease acquisition, multiple execution ranges, partition-aware pruning, full-query memory, and a T-minus-W performance curve remain unproven.

hypothesis: A real Apache object_store client plus a separately reopened quorum-fsynced local authority can preserve intent-before-upload, exact closure-before-root, unknown PUT and authority outcomes, complete reachability, and safe unguarded deletion when a durable per-digest reservation serializes publication against sweep.
learned: Delete-time root revalidation alone is insufficient for backends without native conditional delete. Publication can start after revalidation, verify the old digest object, and race the unguarded delete. A durable per-digest deletion reservation closes that window by rejecting intersecting publication until delete outcome recovery and retirement. The receipt is same-machine and single-process; replicated transaction authority, independent-disk recovery, process kills, provider-native guarded delete, and cloud cost curves remain unproven.

hypothesis: Publication intents, roots, pins, deletion reservations, and durable request outcomes can share the existing three-node OpenRaft generation authority and survive lost replies, real leader-process death, exact retry, generation transition, and restarted-node replay without exposing a stale or conflicting publication decision.
learned: Publication outcome resolution must be linearizable, reader-visible roots and pins need compare-and-swap, and both intents and deletion permits must remain generation-bound in the same replicated state machine. This admits the authority contract only. Publisher and sweeper process death at object-operation boundaries, authority snapshot and outcome expiry, independent-disk loss, provider-native guarded delete, reservation partitioning, and cloud cost curves remain unproven.

hypothesis: A dedicated publisher process can recover from SIGKILL after quorum-durable Prepare and before the first object PUT, restart with empty scratch, replay the exact canonical job and request identities, verify immutable bytes by named reads, and complete one atomic root publication through the replicated cell authority.
learned: Durable publication state is sufficient to restart a publisher without a worker-local journal at the first effect boundary. The immutable job and transition identities must be derived from canonical bytes, and the controller must prove both the replicated Prepare outcome and object absence before killing the first worker. Partial uploads, lost object or Publish replies, abandoned intents, sweeper receipts, object-effect fencing, authority snapshot repair, and cloud semantics remain unproven.

hypothesis: A publisher can recover from SIGKILL after an immutable data-object PUT takes effect but its response becomes retryable-unknown, restart with empty scratch, recover the canonical job from quorum-durable intent, verify the existing named object exactly, complete the closure, and publish one atomic root.
learned: An unknown object-write response must remain uncertain until exact named identity resolves it. Replicated intent plus deterministic immutable names is sufficient to restart without a worker-local journal, but root publication must remain after a full closure walk. Lost manifest and Publish replies, repeated unknown responses, multipart residue, abandoned-intent reassignment, sweeper recovery, generation-bound effect grants, independent-disk loss, and cloud semantics remain unproven.

hypothesis: A publisher can recover from SIGKILL after the immutable manifest PUT takes effect but its response becomes retryable-unknown, restart with empty scratch, recover the canonical job from quorum-durable intent, verify every data object and the manifest by exact named identity, walk the complete closure, and publish one atomic root.
learned: Manifest identity authenticates only manifest bytes. It does not prove child presence. A replacement can recover safely from replicated intent and deterministic immutable names, but it must replay data identities and walk the complete named closure before requesting visibility. Lost Publish replies, repeated unknown responses, multipart residue, abandoned-intent reassignment, sweeper recovery, generation-bound effect grants, independent-disk loss, and cloud semantics remain unproven.

hypothesis: A publisher can recover after its replicated Publish command applies but its response is lost, then the publisher and accepting authority leader die, by reconstructing the stable job and request identity from empty scratch, resolving the quorum-durable outcome on a successor, and retrying without a second authority or object effect.
learned: A matching current root and complete object closure do not identify the outcome of the original Publish invocation. Safe crash recovery requires a replicated command receipt keyed by a stable identity, exact fingerprint validation, and retry that returns the original applied position without a second state transition. Retained-outcome expiry and snapshot restoration, repeated lost replies, later-root supersession, generation handoff, multipart residue, independent-disk loss, and cloud semantics remain unproven.

hypothesis: Pinned SlateDB can establish a correctness-gated local physical incumbent for deterministic ingest, point reads, ordered scans, and fresh-instance reopen while recording backend requests and bytes through the shared eval and OTel contracts.
learned: A fresh-instance reopen was roughly three orders of magnitude slower than a warm-instance read, so cache state must remain a hard gate. The local incumbent is directionally useful but not a product verdict: raw backend calls include expected absence and conditional-operation failures, compaction is not forced, and remote S3, GCS, scale, and named cost ceilings remain unmeasured.

hypothesis: Pinned SlateDB can reopen from a fresh in-process cache without reading work proportional to all durable bytes as a deterministic dataset grows from 1 MiB to 64 MiB.
learned: The original Phase 0 timing blended close writes with recovery and is superseded. With corrected boundaries, 1 MiB and 8 MiB reopen are metadata-bounded, but the 64 MiB open reads 210,773,938 bytes before the first point lookup. This crosses RFC-0022's stop threshold for the untuned SlateDB incumbent. It does not falsify objectKV; it requires one bounded SlateDB layout and compaction pass before replacing that incumbent.

hypothesis: A centralized Cell v0 OCC resolver can emit product-shaped point and range histories that are strict serializable in commit-version order, while an independent oracle detects point conflicts, range phantoms, partial effects, incomplete conflict coverage, and stale read versions.
learned: The transaction contract can now be checked independently at the centralized model boundary. This does not prove the OpenRaft process path, resolver partitioning, commit recovery, or a clean reproducible candidate. Feed the same frozen history schema from the real process client next.

hypothesis: One three-node OpenRaft data group can deterministically enforce Cell v0 point and range conflicts, atomic multi-range mutation, lost-reply outcome recovery, exact retry, and restarted-replica state reconstruction while feeding an independent strict-serializability oracle.
learned: The process composition is semantically viable at the single-group same-machine boundary. The gate exposed an invalid non-empty binary-key JSON map in transaction status and snapshot state; canonical ordered entry arrays plus a backward-compatible empty-map decoder repaired the owning storage contract. Clean admission, automatic elections, bounded conflict retention, snapshot installation, independent failure domains, multi-group coordination, and performance remain open.

hypothesis: A separately cacheable sparse row-object index can make exact cold point reads use one bounded data range GET without LIST or complete-object scanning.
learned: The one-block physical read shape is implementable, and the serving-range checks were within diagnostic noise of the direct indexed reader. A complete-object scan can return exact values while being physically invalid, so semantic correctness and workload admission must remain separate gates. This does not prove scale independence, cloud latency, release performance, concurrency, cost, or the complete MVCC segment algebra.

supersession_reason: The same turn corrected the RAM control profile and added RFC-0003 to the suite contract, changing the suite hash before final receipts were frozen.
hypothesis: A separately cacheable sparse row-object index can make exact cold point reads use one bounded data range GET without LIST or complete-object scanning.
learned: The one-block physical read shape is implementable, and the serving-range checks were within diagnostic noise of the direct indexed reader. A complete-object scan can return exact values while being physically invalid, so semantic correctness and workload admission must remain separate gates. This does not prove scale independence, cloud latency, release performance, concurrency, cost, or the complete MVCC segment algebra.

hypothesis: Within one bounded range, a content-addressed row-object manifest and bounded data objects can hold each exact cold point read to one indexed data range GET and one block of transferred bytes as the range grows from 1 MiB to 64 MiB.
learned: Partitioning the row base into bounded objects keeps measured data request work and bytes flat through the 64 MiB range profile, and the serving boundary remains within diagnostic noise of the direct indexed reader. Metadata warmup grows with segment count, so range splitting must bound each closure and the empty-worker path must fetch only the selected index before its first read. Cloud latency, concurrency, clean-source reproducibility, OTel, scans, compaction, publication economics, and the complete MVCC segment algebra remain unproven.

hypothesis: An empty serving worker can return its first exact point read after one manifest GET, one selected-index GET, and one data range GET without full range hydration.
supersession_reason: The lane selected p99, but the result contract emitted only the median as the primary value. The evaluator was corrected to emit the configured statistic and selected value before the final rerun.
learned: A schema-valid artifact can still report the wrong statistic when the result contract does not bind the lane selector to an emitted value. The configured statistic, selected value, raw samples, median, and MAD must remain distinct fields.

hypothesis: As one assigned range grows from 1 MiB to 64 MiB, an empty serving worker can keep its first exact point read to one manifest GET, one selected-index GET, and one data range GET without full range hydration.
learned: Across a 63.96x complete-closure increase, lazy first-read response bytes grew 1.19x and p99 grew 1.03x, while full restore grew with closure and was 276.11x slower at 64 MiB. The manifest-first selected-index path is locally implementable. Cloud latency, process replacement, authoritative root open, txLog replay, scans, concurrency, clean-source reproducibility, OTel, and cost remain unproven.

hypothesis: After a serving process is killed, a distinct empty-scratch replacement can discover the replicated authoritative row root and logical txLog root, quorum-recover a non-empty suffix, and return exact base and tail reads without complete range hydration.
learned: The object-base plus durable-tail recovery equation is executable across an operating-system process kill and a distinct empty-scratch replacement. The candidate used one manifest, one index, one range GET, and 3.36 percent of the encoded closure, while full hydration was 1.67x slower at p99 and transferred 29.96x more bytes. Skipping the required tail produced nine anomalies. The local three-file adapter is not the production OpenRaft data txLog; independent hosts, concurrent catch-up, range semantics, cloud latency, clean-source admission, and economics remain open.

supersession_reason: Promoting RFC-0026 and the suite to evaluating changed the frozen contract bytes after the preliminary v1 receipts. The v2 run binds the same implementation and seeds to the exact current contract hash.
hypothesis: After a serving process is killed, a distinct empty-scratch replacement can discover the replicated authoritative row root and logical txLog root, quorum-recover a non-empty suffix, and return exact base and tail reads without complete range hydration.
learned: The current contract reproduces the object-base plus durable-tail recovery result across an operating-system process kill and a distinct empty-scratch replacement. The lazy path was 1.68x faster at p99 and moved 29.96x fewer object bytes than full hydration. Skipping the tail produced nine anomalies. The local three-file adapter is not the production OpenRaft data txLog; independent hosts, concurrent catch-up, range semantics, cloud latency, clean-source admission, and economics remain open.

supersession_reason: The first implementation started recovery.first_correct_read_duration after catch-up and optional full hydration. Those receipts measured only final point reads and do not satisfy the metric contract. The v2 timer begins at worker-process entry.

hypothesis: A distinct empty-scratch replacement worker can reconstruct ObjectState(O) plus an authority-owned OpenRaft retained transaction stream through a frozen target, then perform a second bounded catch-up while commits continue without reading physical Raft journal paths.
learned: The recovery seam no longer depends on LocalReplicatedWal or a physical OpenRaft journal path. A linearizable paginated state-machine stream preserved exact target snapshots across Raft index gaps and a second catch-up round. Candidate recovery was 1.64x faster at p99 and moved 6.85x fewer object bytes than full hydration on this 39 KiB local closure. This does not prove safe-pop, bounded retained bytes, independent-machine durability, GCS behavior, overload convergence, serving-lease activation, release performance, OTel, or production economics.

hypothesis: At fixed live key cardinality and ideal objectification O=C, removing the complete retained recovery stream is sufficient to keep the current serialized transaction-authority state within 2x growth from 256 to 4096 lifetime commits.
learned: Object-frontier safe pop can reclaim only recovery commands. The current authority also retains lifetime-growing OCC history, durable retry outcomes, request fingerprints, and user values. Split those state domains by minimum read version, retry floor, serving coverage, and object-durable frontier before implementing safe pop.

hypothesis: At fixed live key cardinality, independently advancing the minimum admitted read version R and per-client retry floor Q while projecting ideal object frontier O=C keeps complete transaction-authority state within 2x growth from 256 to 4096 lifetime commits.
learned: The split-frontier state shape removes lifetime-commit growth without hiding omitted state. It does not improve the sequential sync-per-entry process path, which delivered only about 30 measured commits per second including cluster setup and failed the fixed execution budget. Authenticate O and add crash-safe pop, then test commit batching under an independent performance suite.

hypothesis: A pending immutable object closure plus a data-voter quorum certificate can make physical recovery-stream pop crash-safe without placing object I/O on the foreground commit path.
learned: The application retained recovery stream can be physically bounded without object access on transaction acknowledgement. Pending publication state protects the closure across pop and activation crashes. This does not purge the internal OpenRaft journal or admit commit throughput, independent-machine durability, cloud object behavior, or production signer operations.

hypothesis: Submitting independent transaction requests through a bounded concurrency window lets OpenRaft and the stable journal group durable appends enough to reach at least 200 transactions per second, at most 250 ms p99, and at least 4x the same-durability sequential control without changing strict-serializable recovery semantics.
learned: Bounded concurrency yields useful pipelining and follower append coalescing, but the leader still synchronizes one stable append per transaction. The mechanism is not sufficient as objectKV group commit. Preserve the I/O instrumentation and recovery checks, then test an explicit commit-proxy batch entry under the same durability control.

hypothesis: One explicit Raft application entry containing 16 independently retryable transactions can reach at least 400 durable transactions per second, at most 100 ms p99, at least eight logical transactions per leader append, and at least 2.5x the same-durability one-entry control while preserving ordered versionstamps, conflict semantics, pagination, exact retry, failover, and restart.
learned: The leader synchronization bottleneck can be amortized without collapsing transactions into one application atomic unit. A FoundationDB-style shared commit version plus batch order preserves per-transaction identity and ordered recovery while reducing the measured leader append count from 512 to 32. The mechanism now needs delay, byte, overload, conflict, fairness, objectification-convergence, clean-source, and independent-media gates.

hypothesis: A bounded commit proxy with 16 items, 64 callers, a 2 ms delay, and a 256 KiB entry cap can start from independent client requests and reach at least 500 durable transactions per second, at most 100 ms p99, at least eight logical transactions per leader append, and at least 2.5x the same-durability one-entry control while preserving exact retry, replay, failover, restart, byte, sparse, and overload semantics.
learned: Starting from independent requests preserved the transaction contract, but a 16-item batch at 64 callers formed a second queue wave and crossed the frozen p99 ceiling. The 32-caller control isolated the local admission knee. Discard this exact configuration rather than weaken the latency gate.

hypothesis: A separately frozen 32-item commit-proxy batch at 64 callers can reach at least 900 durable transactions per second, at most 100 ms p99, at least 16 logical transactions per leader append, and at least 4x the same-durability one-entry control while preserving independent request, byte, sparse, overload, retry, replay, failover, and restart semantics.
learned: The bounded independent-request proxy can amortize local leader synchronization without exposing batch identity to clients. The retained 32-item shape clears the local latency and throughput gates, while the compact v2 wire keeps the 128 KiB byte control at eight 8 KiB-value transactions. It now requires conflict and concurrent object-frontier stress before clean independent-media execution.

hypothesis: A 32-item independent-request commit proxy can resolve a deterministic 25 percent conflict suffix while an authenticated immutable object frontier advances through frozen O, reconstruct exact final state from ObjectState(O) plus txLog(O,C], and clear 700 outcomes per second, 150 ms p99, 16 outcomes per leader append, and 4x the same-durability one-entry control.
learned: Concurrent authenticated objectification does not erase the local batching advantage or corrupt the retained suffix at this scale. The exact object-plus-tail equation survives controlled conflict, both authority failovers, voter restart, and fresh-client recovery. Independent failure domains, remote objects, repeated frontier convergence, physical OpenRaft journal reclamation, clean-source reproducibility, OTel, and economics remain unproven.

hypothesis: A three-process OpenRaft data quorum can durably snapshot complete state, reject purge above snapshot coverage, canonical-compact physical journals, stop every process, reopen exact state plus retained suffix, replay one exact retry, and accept a new suffix commit.
learned: The crash-safe process maintenance mechanism works and the physical journal is no longer the dominant retained-media source. Without aligned resolver, retry, and authenticated object frontiers, complete replicated snapshots retain lifetime recovery and retry state and reach 38.66082x physical amplification. The next gate must compose real R, bounded Q(client), and O transitions before snapshot and repeat the cycle before any independent-media claim.

hypothesis: Four process cycles aligned on resolver frontier R, a 64-request retry frontier Q(client), and authenticated object frontier O can preserve exact retry and object-plus-suffix recovery while holding complete six-process snapshot plus retained-journal media below 8x one logical copy and cycle-four snapshot bytes below 1.25x cycle one.
learned: Aligned R, Q(client), and O frontiers bound the lifetime curve but do not make the current replicated state representation economical. The no-Q control proves the retry frontier is necessary. Complete-media accounting shows that the remaining problem is the snapshot ownership and encoding constant factor, not retained journal growth. Before independent-media execution, compare compact row, random-access columnar, and multi-layout manifested run shapes against the same point, scan, recovery, and media contracts.

hypothesis: One manifested MVCC history can support exact indexed row, indexed Parquet, and hybrid columnar reads while exposing the point, scan, media, compaction, and branching costs that decide whether columnar compacted runs belong in the objectKV permanent base.
learned: A shared manifested history remains credible, but selected Parquet row groups plus projection are not a competitive generic point path. Parquet improved projected scan throughput 1.873x while multiplying point requests by 10 and bytes by 16.35x. The row-capsule hybrid reduced requests but used 1.925x the row control's stored-to-live media. Continue only with random-access columnar, authenticated request coalescing, or an honestly accounted typed sidecar against the unchanged row control.

hypothesis: A manifested run that stores the exact MVCC row capsule once and duplicates only the typed analytical projection can preserve indexed-row point economics while producing a materially faster columnar scan path with bounded durable, compaction, and resident-index amplification.
learned: The honestly counted split layout passed every frozen local admission gate and is the first credible typed object-run mechanism. It is a multi-layout manifested source of truth, not plain Parquet: exact values and MVCC versions live in the row capsule, while only analytical columns are duplicated. Two isolated outlier runs preceded the frozen alternating nine-sample comparison; backend timing showed no stable layout-specific penalty, so repeated alternation is now part of the contract. Clean-source reproducibility, real GCS request latency, cold-cache behavior, object economics, Vortex, recovery from the split closure, and DataFusion base-plus-tail execution remain unproven.

hypothesis: A permanent columnar MVCC layout with a compact resident key-range index, independently checksummed projection stripes and opaque payload pages, and a bounded disposable RangeEngine cache can preserve exact point and restart semantics while beating indexed row objects on transferred bytes, p99, projected scans, and total media.
learned: The HANA-like mechanism is locally credible: one durable columnar base can serve exact MVCC points through a compact key-to-stripe index, stream projections without opaque values, rebuild after discarding all serving state, and stay near row-object media. The unresolved risk moved from local format mechanics to remote two-request latency, cache eviction under a larger working set, concurrent L1 and L2 merge semantics, and direct Arrow/DataFusion execution.

hypothesis: A custom DataFusion source can execute exact projected SQL directly over the C5 columnar object while using point-sized logical stripes, bounded coalesced scan range GETs, incremental Arrow batches, and zero opaque payload reads.
learned: The direct DataFusion path works, but point-sized stripes alone create unacceptable remote scan request amplification. Bounded 256 KiB scan coalescing reduced projection requests by 32.61x, doubled local SQL throughput, and preserved exact per-stripe checksum validation and small Arrow batches. Payload prefetch is independently visible and costly. The remaining architecture risks are exact live-tail invalidation, complete-query memory, parallel range scheduling, and real GCS latency.

hypothesis: At 20 percent cache coverage and Zipf alpha 1.4, bounded ghost two-chance admission preserves the reusable point hot set across a full projected scan better than full admission while preserving exact MVCC results and the byte capacity bound.
learned: Cache policy is a material part of the C5 serving architecture. Ghost two-chance pays more misses during scan pollution but preserves the reusable point hot set and reduces subsequent object requests. This does not replace the required full cache-ratio, skew, phase-shift, concurrent-request, publication-debt, and recovery matrix.

hypothesis: The CloudJump-inspired ghost two-chance effect remains observable through the real GCS adapter and namespaced immutable C5 media on a bounded one-seed canary.
learned: The objectKV GCS adapter and namespaced C5 layout execute end to end, and admission policy changes remote request and latency cost. The earlier 16,384-key nine-repeat serial profile was stopped after five minutes at its first sample, showing that the full cloud curve needs concurrent scheduling and a bounded canary before scale. Clean source, OTel, multiple seeds, larger dataset-to-cache ratios, phase shifts, authority conformance, and an all-fast-tier same-durability control remain open.

hypothesis: The public okv::SingleRange boundary can commit through the replicated transaction authority, preserve every retained record when pagination ends inside a shared commit version, serve exact object-base-plus-tail reads, and recover in a distinct empty process after the first process is killed.
learned: The repository now has one application-callable continuous objectKV slice instead of evaluator-only components. Batch-aware recovery is required after RFC-0032, and the one-record page test preserved both same-version items. This is not a complete cell: clean OTel replay, independently durable voters, activation leases, scans, objectification ownership, and multi-range routing remain open.

hypothesis: The public okv::SingleRange boundary can preserve the exact object-base-plus-txLog recovery equation through a real GCS object backend, a killed serving process, an empty replacement, and required OTel without expanding its bounded named-object read path.
learned: The public single-range composition is backend-generic in practice, not only by trait signature. A real GCS base preserved exact recovery and one-manifest, one-index, one-range, zero-LIST access. Remote latency is material but the current 756.950 ms timer combines process start, three authority reads, txLog catch-up, and object work from an uncontrolled Mac, so the next useful result is request-level spans and repeated matched local/GCS runs on R0, not a larger cell.

hypothesis: A complete immutable object base can activate a bounded disposable RocksDB serving image below the public SingleRange API, preserve exact object-base-plus-txLog semantics after process replacement, and serve a measured steady-state point-read window without object operations.
learned: The SSD-shaped serving path now functions through the public kernel rather than only in the direct RocksDB prototype. The diagnostic reached 824252 reads/s at 1583 ns p99 with zero object operations after activation. The earlier direct RocksDB diagnostic was about 1.29M reads/s, so the current public path has a roughly 36 percent throughput tax that must be decomposed before admission. No NVMe performance claim is valid until a clean optimized ABBA batch records an explicit provider device.

finding: The diagnostic scratch volume /dev/disk3s5 is APFS on physical store disk0s2, backed by the internal APPLE SSD AP1024Z NVMe device. This upgrades the mechanism statement to NVMe-backed, but does not change the inconclusive performance verdict because the build was debug, source was dirty, the dataset was small, and the machine was not load-isolated.

hypothesis: After generation-fenced admission from a GCS object base and retained txLog suffix, the public SingleRange RocksDB serving path remains within 20 percent of direct RocksDB throughput and p99 on the same local NVMe machine.

machine.hot_scratch: 375 GiB GCP local SSD, NVMe, ext4

learned: The object-native recovery and zero-object resident-read mechanism works on real GCS plus local NVMe, but the composed public read path is not yet competitive with direct RocksDB. The first optimization target is the 26.37 percent throughput and 41.91 percent p99 tax. The harness also needs reusable frozen fixtures before scale and an executable secondary-metric p99 comparison before the next admission.

hypothesis: Removing repeated manifest location and object-reference cloning from complete-image point reads will bring the public SingleRange path within 20 percent of direct RocksDB throughput and p99.

machine.hot_scratch: 375 GiB GCP local SSD, NVMe, ext4

learned: Repeated manifest routing materially reduced throughput, but it did not explain tail latency. The wrapper now clears throughput by less than one percentage point in each order while p99 remains 30 to 35 percent worse. Move generation, coverage, and closure checks to activation and frontier transitions, materialize the suffix in the resident engine, and test an engine-native lookup before advancing the stack.

hypothesis: A native resident engine that moves generation, range, closure, MVCC, and retained-tail semantics into RocksDB can remain within 20 percent of an owned-value direct RocksDB control for throughput and p99 while preserving exact object-base-plus-txLog recovery.

machine.hot_scratch: 375 GiB GCP local SSD, NVMe, ext4

learned: The native engine preserved exact recovery and zero-object steady-state reads, but it failed the frozen p99 ceiling in both process orders.
